summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted directly from clinic with recurrent epigastric pain, nausea, and vomiting, one month after a prior hospitalization for similar symptoms. With a history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube placement due to a previous GJ anastomotic ulcer, she was kept NPO, given IV fluids, IV proton-pump inhibitor, and IV morphine for pain. Tube feeds were restarted at a reduced rate and gradually tolerated. Her symptoms improved significantly over four days, with no signs of infection or organ dysfunction on labs. She was discharged home in stable condition on continuous tube feeds at 50 cc/hr, with instructions to continue home medications, use oxycodone for breakthrough pain, and follow up with surgery and GI. No procedures were performed during this admission.
